name: Prism Sound
_legal_entity: Audio Squadron Limited, trading as Prism Sound. Its footer reads « (c) 2026 Audio Squadron Ltd. All rights reserved. »
_terms_read_and_permitting: Measured 2026-11-25. prismsound.io publishes NO terms-of-use page - six likely paths all 404, and the full 74-page sitemap lists only a privacy policy and one PDF. That PDF, « Audio Squadron Limited Terms & Conditions of Sale », is a 7-page image-only scan read page by page: all 19 clauses, and none forbids copying or reusing content. Its nearest clauses do not reach website material. robots.txt on both hosts permits every product and spec path. So the sale terms were genuinely read and permit this, while the website-use question has no document to answer it - a mixed state worth naming, because it is neither « read and permitted » nor « no page found ».
_the_maker_disclaims_its_own_figures: Clause 6(b) of the sale terms, which no other brand in this catalogue states: « The Seller shall use reasonable endeavours to ensure the accuracy of technical data or literature relating to the goods, but the Seller accepts no liability [...] for any error or omission in such technical data or literature. » Every spec page adds « specifications are subject to amendment without notice. E&OE. » The figures remain the best source there is; this is simply the one maker that puts the caveat in a contract.
_no_chip_part_number_anywhere: A grep across every captured Prism Sound page for AK4, ES90, CS43, PCM17, WM87, Sabre, Burr-Brown, Asahi Kasei and Cirrus Logic returned ZERO matches. Nine records under this brand and not one converter part number, which is unusual at this level - and means `family` is absent on every one of them.
_the_host_connection_is_never_specified: Titan, Atlas, Lyra 1, Lyra 2 and Orpheus publish no USB or FireWire sample-rate or bit-depth figure at all: the host port appears only as a connector count under Rear Panel. The only rate quotable for them is « System sample rates » from the Synchronization section, which is not labelled a USB ceiling and is not recorded as one. Callia is the single exception, and it is also the single product whose USB ceiling exceeds its S/PDIF ceiling - 384 kHz / 32 bit / DSD128 against 192 kHz / 24 bit / DSD64.
_could_not_reach: The product brochure at /product-brochure/ is a third-party JavaScript flip-book (paperturn-view.com) whose shell carries no page text and no direct PDF link; it needs a browser session and was not guessed at. Per-product datasheet PDFs do not exist - the Downloads page of every product links only the sale terms. The ADA-128's MADI module specification is published as « [Under development] ».
